newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua authorises storm repairs to coffee roads.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua authorises storm repairs to coffee roads.

text.p: Nicaragua authorized the immediate repair of roads damaged by heavy rains brought by Tropical Storm Marco in an effort to protect the 1996-97 coffee cycle, a top official said on Friday.

"The Transportaion Ministry has been authorized by the president to immediately start repairing the damaged roads, if climatic conditions permit," Vice Minister of Agriculture Salvador Robelo told a news conference.
"If the measures are taken in time, and the rain doesn't continue, the roads can be repaired and the coffee moved out," he said.

The head of the Nicaragua Coffee Association (Unicafe), David Robleto, said if the government does not repair the roads immediately, 560,000 quintales, or more than half Nicaragua's exportable coffee harvest, could be in danger of being lost.
"Coffee production has been in danger since the first hurricane (Hurricane Cesar in July) passed through and the only thing that can be done is repair the roads, rapidly," he said.
He said Unicafe still has not quantified the total damage, and will release a report on Monday.

Robelo said the recent rains produced mature beans to fall from trees and also delayed the ripening of maturing beans, setting back the harvest. But he added the effects were limited, stressing the main threat to the coffee harvest was the destruction of roads in coffee- growing regions.
Nicaragua is projected to produce 1,215,867 quintales (100- lb or 46-kg bags) of coffee in 1996-97, exporting 1,033,487 quintales, Robleto said.
Tropical Storm Marco formed off Nicaragua's coast late on Sunday and before heading northeast towards the Caribbean Islands. It has produced heavy rains throughout Nicaragua for the entire week.
